aisec: Research shows agents face prompt injection via exposed conversation history, poisoned skill supply chains, multi-step attacks, and resource-exhaustion abuse; new defenses include system-call mediation and bounded autonomy.
UK's cyber agency says AI-driven attacks mostly succeed by exploiting long-neglected basic weaknesses, while Unit 42 documents autonomous AI agents automating intrusions across multiple platforms.
CrowdStrike's proposed $44 billion Zscaler purchase aims at stronger control of AI agents, as red-teaming research questions benchmark reliability and attacker diversity.
ai: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia after resigning amid reported misconduct dominates coverage, raising governance questions at a central AI hardware supplier.
OpenAI and Cisco announced Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime protecting live systems during patch rollout; OpenAI customer stories highlight enterprise agent adoption in legal and support.
Z.ai released GLM 5.4 with a looped transformer, DeepMind paired agents with formal verification for quantum algorithms, and NVIDIA released cuDSS 1.0 and GPU-accelerated DuckDB tooling.
cyber: Iran-aligned Volant Manticore uses the IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor against Cyprus telecoms, airlines and infrastructure, while Broadcom patched 23 VMware flaws including a 9.8-rated vCenter authentication bypass.
Industrial serial gateways expose whether authentication protects them, and Project Zero revisited VirtualBox's Windows process hardening, highlighting exposure in OT and virtualization software.
Kirsten Davies became Acting National Cyber Director, a researcher unmasked a decade of ransomware aliases, and Schneier argued recent outages reflect underinvestment in infrastructure.
